The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Community interest provides the Public
Safety Commission with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 3rd Monday of every month.

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires
a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact
the Public Safety Commission via email at fire@cityofsanmarino.org or by phone at (626) 300-
0735 prior to the meeting for assistance.

  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361 (AB 361)
Members of the Public Safety Commission may teleconference into the meeting without noticing
each teleconference location from which a member will be participating in a public meeting.

  CORONAVIRUS DISEASE (COVID-19) ADVISORY
As a precaution to protect staff, our constituents, and appointed officials, the City is following
the State and County Health Department’s current Health Officer recommendations to prevent
and reduce transmission of COVID0-19 by holding meetings via teleconference

Members of the public may observe and offer comment at this meeting telephonically or
otherwise electronically:

  the meeting, prior to the close of public comment on an item, to be read by the
  Committee during public comment. Lengthy public comment may be summarized in the
  interest of time.

 TO:  Chair and Members of the Public Safety Commission

FROM:  John N. Incontro, Police Chief

DATE:  August 15, 2022

SUBJECT:  POLICE DEPARTMENT UPDATE REPORT JULY 2022

BACKGROUND

Each month, the San Marino Police Department provides a brief and informational update on
crime, traffic issues, and other items of interest to the public and to the Public Safety Committee.

DISCUSSION

As of July 31, 2022, the Detective Bureau completed the following activities:

•  13 filings were submitted to the district attorney’s office for review
•  Two of these cases were denied filing due to the L.A. County D.A.'s special directive
order. One case was related to a subject being intoxicated in public. The other case was for a
subject with a suspended license.
•  One search warrant for a medical record was authored for an on-going investigation.

Since July 1, 2022, there were two residential burglaries, one attempted residential burglary and
one commercial burglary. In early July, a residence was armed with an alarm while the residents
were not home. An unknown suspect smashed two rear family room windows to gain entry
inside the home. The call from the alarm company to PD dispatch was delayed by approximately
10 minutes. Some alarm companies have a protocol to contact the homeowner prior to
dispatching per the homeowner’s request. Officers arrived on scene to set up a perimeter. No
suspects were located in the area. The home was ransacked by the suspect. There were no
surveillance cameras at the home or in the area. No lost was reported as of date.

Officers also responded to another residential burglary investigation. The residents were not
home at the time of the incident. When, the resident returned home, the resident observed a
bedroom ransacked. Officers responded to the location and discovered the rear facing kitchen
window screen was removed and the window was pushed open. A possible latent print was
located however, the print appeared to be consistent with an individual wearing a glove. This
residence did not have surveillance cameras and did not have an alarm system.

  6 of 30
 The attempted burglary investigation was conducted on an unoccupied residence listed for sale.
Officers responded to the location and met with the daughter of the homeowner. Officers
determined access was not made inside the residence.

Officers also responded to an audible alarm activation at a dentist office. Officers arrived on scene
and determined the suspect used an unknown object to smash a window located in the front of
the property. Officers conducted an interior check but no one was located inside of the business.
The unknown suspect ransacked a drawer behind the front counter taking an unknown amount
of gift cards. There were surveillance cameras at the business but they were inoperable.

Also in July, a resident reported two suspicious subjects observed on surveillance camera in the
rear yard of the residence. Officers responded to the residence and set up a perimeter to safely
contain the area. A Honda SUV was located parked in the driveway. Officers conducted a record
check and determined the vehicle was stolen. A report of a subject in the nearby Huntington
Library was received by dispatch. Officers located the subject who match the description of one
of the two outstanding subjects in the Huntington Library property. A subject riding a bicycle in
the area was also located. Officers determined this subject was the other outstanding suspect.
The bicycle was determined to be stolen from another residence’s garage. These two subjects
were apprehended and booked at Pasadena City Jail on burglary, theft and stolen vehicle charges.
During the month of July, there were 31 FLOCK automated license plate reader alert
notifications. These notifications included misreads or vehicles not removed from the stolen
vehicle database by the originating agency. Officers pursued each notification as a possible stolen
vehicle and searched the area until otherwise notified.

The FLOCK cameras are not only a useful tool to locate stolen vehicles but have helped with
follow up investigations. Officers and Detectives are able to locate suspect vehicles by searching
vehicle images through the FLOCK database.

Our analysis indicates that there is no specific pattern or location selected for the above incidents.
The point of entry for these incidents was the rear of the home and to the front at the commercial
burglary. This information will assist us in our crime prevention efforts. We have provided the
information to residents via the Neighborhood Watch Block Captains, police department
website, e-mail and social media. Additionally, we are working on crime suppression strategies
to reduce these crimes. We continue to see an overall decrease in residential burglaries as
compared to previous years.

  7 of 30
 Community Engagement

In the month of July, the Police Department held two community engagement events. On July 10,
2022, Sergeant Bestpitch and Officer Serrano attended a Neighborhood Watch block party. Cone
with a Cop was held on July 28, 2022 at Swirlz and the Police Department gave out 47 cones
while engaging with the community.

Personnel

The department currently has all 28 sworn positions filled. We continue to pursue interested
police officer applicants, in the event a vacancy arises. There are still three cadet position
vacancies. We have one cadet and one police officer applicant that will be starting the background
process.

Technology

In the coming months, staff will be presenting City Council with an agreement for California
POST approved self-paced mobile training software, offered by Performa Labs, Inc. Performa Labs
leverages technology and innovation to improve peace officer safety, and increase safety to the
community we serve. The training software empowers peace officers to make decisions in critical
or life-threatening situations. The software can be used on a variety of devices and doesn’t require
the officer to travel to a classroom or attend a scheduled webinar.

Traffic

The Office of Traffic Safety grant requires the department to conduct a number of traffic safety
operations during the grant period and they provide the funding for the event. On Saturday,
August 6, 2022 members of the San Marino Police Department, in collaboration with police
officers from Vernon Police Department and Mothers Against Drunk Driving (MADD),
conducted a Driving Under the Influence/Driver’s License Checkpoint. During the checkpoint
five individuals were cited for operating a vehicle while unlicensed or with a suspended,
revoked license. A total of 1,073 vehicles passed through the checkpoint, and an additional 408
vehicles were contacted during the operation.

  8 of 30
 Traffic Enforcement

Traffic enforcement is based upon three categories; traffic complaints from the community,
observation of violations by officers, and traffic collision data. The Department maintains a list of
traffic complaint locations and traffic collision data for traffic enforcement. As part of our traffic
collision investigations, we will look for other issues that may have been a contributory factor in
the collision. Those factors could be distracted driving, engineering, or environmental.

Below are the top collision locations of July 2022

  1.  Huntington Drive- Four Collisions
  2.  Los Robles Avenue- Two Collisions
  3.  Granada Avenue- Two Collisions

Below are the top factors of collisions of July 2022

  1.  CVC 22350 - Speeding – Four Collisions
  2.  CVC 22450 – Cell Phone – Two locations

Moving Violations

The patrol division is continuing maximum efforts in place of the motor officers in answering all
traffic complaints and covering primary collision areas. Even with patrol providing coverage in
these places of importance, the coverage is significantly less due to the promotion of our two
motor officers. Year-to-date the department has issued 965 moving citations.

 TO:  Chair and Members of the Public Safety Commission

 FROM:  M. D. Rueda, Fire Chief

 DATE:  August 15, 2022

 SUBJECT:  FIRE DEPARTMENT MONTHLY REPORT

BACKGROUND

The San Marino Fire Department completes a monthly report for the Public Safety Commission,
providing an overview of department activities, significant incidents, and monthly statistics.

DISCUSSION

Annual Commercial and Target Hazard Inspections
During the month of August, the Fire Department will begin annual fire inspections of all
commercial facilities and properties designated by the Fire Department as posing significant risk.
Inspections will include all public facilities, schools, churches, and the Huntington Library.

Chinese Club First Aid Safety Course
The San Marino Fire Department hosted a First Aid & Safety class for members of the Chinese
Club on Thursday, July 28. Attendees of the class were taught first aid skills, including CPR, active
bleeding, and use of tourniquets; use of fire extinguishers; and utility shutoffs. The Fire
Department plans to conduct additional safety courses this year for all residents to attend.

Significant Incidents
On July 4, the San Marino Fire Department responded to multiple incidents in Lacy Park during
the Fourth of July festivities. Reserve Engine 91 and a medcart on loan from the San Gabriel Fire
Department were assigned to Lacy Park for the duration of the event. The medcart allows
firefighter/paramedics to respond to medical emergencies where large crowds would prohibit
quick response by the rescue ambulance. The San Marino Fire Department received approval to
purchase its own medcart as part of the current fiscal year’s capital equipment budget. Frontline
RA91 and E91 remained available to respond to incidents occurring in the City during the Fourth
of July event. E91 patrolled the streets surrounding Lacy Park during the fireworks show to
monitor for potential fires caused by fallout.

On July 28, Engine 91, along with units from Alhambra, Pasadena, South Pasadena, and San Gabriel
responded to a residential structure fire at a vacant home under construction at 1212 Roanoke
Road. Engine 91 arrived on scene and reported an approximately 3000 square foot home involved
with a significant fire in the walls and attic spaces. With the assistance of our neighboring agencies,

  14 of 30
 San Marino firefighters were successful in confining the fire to the structure of origin. Residents
on either side of the home and to the rear were initially evacuated in an abundance of caution,
but were quickly allowed to return to their homes. Due to the fire in the attic and walls,
extinguishing the fire took well over an hour. There was no damage to any adjacent homes, and
no injuries. Cause of the fire appears to be the result of construction taking place.

The San Marino Police Department issued a Nixle Alert during the incident notifying residents to
avoid the area due to Police and Fire activity.

FY 2022-23 Department Objectives
  • Complete the Lexipol implementation of fire department policies and procedures.
  • Accept delivery of the new RA 91.
  • Conduct a review of the current Community Emergency Response Training (CERT) and
  develop a “Citizen Fire Academy” for residents’ participation.
  • Conduct Fire Department First Aid Community Instructional Workshops.
  • Begin construction on the Fire Department’s bathroom renovation.
  • Develop and conduct emergency operations, active shooter training partnered with a
  consultant and the Huntington Library staff.
  • Present the City’s revised Emergency Operations Plan to the Disaster Council and City
  Council for approval.
  • Update the City’s Disaster Cache Inventory.
  • Complete the EOC upgrade.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends the Commission receive and file the Fire Department Monthly Report. If the
Commission concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

“I move to receive and file the Fire Department Monthly Report.”

 TO:  Mayor and City Council

FROM:  M. D. Rueda, Fire Chief

DATE:  August 9, 2022

SUBJECT:  FIRE DEPARTMENT MONTHLY PERFORMANCE REPORT

The attached San Marino Fire Department July 2022 Performance Report represents the incident
data reports intended to meet the Improvement Goals referenced in the March 2, 2018 Report
to City Council titled; Implementation Plan Fire Department Deployment Study. The Fire
Department has been working closely with the Verdugo Fire Communications Center (Verdugo)
to ensure the accuracy of the data being reported. Some of the data sets are not currently
available from Verdugo and are listed as N/A. Verdugo has been made aware of the San Marino
Fire Department’s interest in pursuing the data associated with the fire and life safety goals as
approved by the City Council.

Improvement Goal A in the Report recommended the following:

Call Processing Goals
9-1-1 calls will be answered at the primary PSAP (Public Safety Answering Point) San Marino
Police Department within 15 seconds, 95% of the time.

9-1-1 calls will be transferred from the primary PSAP to Verdugo within 30 seconds from the
time answered, 95% of the time.
This data is not available.

Recommended Turnout Goal
Response personnel shall initiate the response of a unit capable of mitigating an incident to a
priority fire and rescue incident 80 seconds from notification 90% of the time.

Response personnel shall initiate response to all other priority incidents within 60 seconds from
notification 90% of the time.

Recommended First-Due Response Time Goal
The first response unit capable of initiating effective incident intervention shall arrive at a priority
fire or rescue incident within 5 minutes and 20 seconds from notification of response personnel,
90 percent of the time.

  16 of 30
 The first response unit capable of initiating effective incident intervention shall arrive at all other
priority incidents within 5 minutes from notification of response personnel, 90% of the time.

Recommended Response Force Goal
The full effective response force shall arrive at a moderate risk structure fire within 9 minutes
and 20 seconds of notification of response personnel, 90% of the time.
This data is not available.

Cardiac Arrest Data
The Cardiac Arrest data set includes the total number of cardiac arrest patients treated by
Firefighter/Paramedics. We always pray that the number is as low as possible. The more
important data sets are the subsequent measures which include the number of times the
Firefighter/Paramedics are successful in returning a patient’s spontaneous circulation (ROSC) –
our goal with ROSC is always 100%. Saving lives is why the Fire Department exists; unfortunately,
this is not always in our control. Lastly, the subsequent data sets measure the percentages of
correct treatments performed by the Firefighter/Paramedics.

 TO:  Chair Boozell and members of the Public Safety Commission

FROM:  Robert Newman, Interim Director of Parks & Public Works/City Engineer

DATE:  August 15, 2022

SUBJECT:  JULY THROUGH AUGUST PARKS AND PUBLIC WORKS UPDATE

BACKGROUND

Please accept the following as a summary of notable activities that have been accomplished, are
underway or are planned for the balance of this month through your next regularly scheduled
commission meeting.

DISCUSSION

Follow-up Items from Prior Commission Meetings
•  Striping modifications on Huntington Drive westbound between Monterey Road and
  Westhaven Road is still under review by the City’s traffic engineer. A design is expected to
  be shared with the Commission at a future meeting.
•  Iteris is working to complete its Citywide traffic circulation study, including incorporating
  residential survey results, improvement prioritization, and additional conceptual designs for
  the intersection of Huntington Drive at Sierra Madre Boulevard/San Marino Avenue. Staff
  recently met with Iteris to get a progress update. During this meeting, they indicated that
  they anticipate this study will be ready to share with the Commission in the fall.
•  The traffic concerns raised by residents on Bellhaven Road at a previous Commission meeting
  is still pending. Staff is recommending this be addressed after the Citywide Traffic Circulation
  Study is approved by City Council.

Projects in or near Construction
•  Mariposa Landscaping has continued its scheduled work in its Multi-Year Tree Maintenance
  Contract for FY 22-23. To this point, they have planted approximately 70 new trees at
  various locations throughout the City, performed removal of trees approved by the City
  Council, trimmed palm trees citywide, and trimmed trees at Lacy Park in preparation for the
  4th of July celebration. They are also currently performing grid trimming of right-of-way trees
  north of Huntington Drive from Virginia Road westbound to City limits, as well as performing

  21 of 30
   a one-time cleanup of City medians. Beginning this week, Mariposa will be trimming the
  oleanders along Huntington Drive, which will require the closure of the right lane for parts
  of the day.
•  Construction for this fiscal year’s street rehabilitation program project is currently scheduled
  to begin later this month. A total of 31 City streets are scheduled to be resurfaced based on
  the Council-adopted pavement management plan (see Attachment 1 for map of streets). The
  restriping work on Sierra Madre Boulevard that was previously discussed at a Commission
  meeting has been incorporated into the project’s scope of work.
•  Construction for the FY 22-23 sidewalk replacement program is expected to begin in the fall.
  This program replaces approximately 1.0 mile of sidewalk each year at various locations
  throughout the City.
•  At its July 29th meeting, the City Council awarded a construction contract to CABD
  Construction, as well as a construction management contract to Griffin Structures for the
  San Marino Center Renovation. Construction is expected to begin in September.
Projects in Design/Out-to-Bid

•  The Department received a request to study the signage on West Drive at Sherwood Road
  and at Lorain Road for the purposes of highlighting pedestrian activity at these intersections.
  The Department has updated several signs with the current labeling and colors for signs and
  has completed the refreshing of existing ladder crosswalk striping in the near future.
•  Rubio Medina Architects, the consultant for the Fire Station Bathroom Remodel Project, has
  continued their design work on the project.
•  Dudek engineers continue to work on the plans to upgrade of our 3 sanitary sewer lift stations
  as part of the lift station improvement program. They are at the 95% design plans stage.
  Advertisement for construction bids is planned for later this year.

Projects under Study/Analysis

•  The Department has been placing W11-15 signs (see nearby) along certain
  residential streets. [No update to report]

Maintenance Activities
  W11-15 Sign
•  Replaced fallen stop and speed limit signs
•  Repaired sprinklers and irrigation pipes on City medians
•  Placed 84 street pole banners for the San Marino Motor Classic
•  Provided staff support to the Police and Fire Departments at the National Night Out event

  22 of 30
 •  Continued other regularly scheduled summer maintenance activities

Other Department Activities

•  The Department recently completed successful recruitments for the positions of Maintenance
  Worker I, as well as Urban Forester. Recruitment for one additional Maintenance Worker I
  is still ongoing.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Commission receive and file this report. If the Commission concurs
with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

“I move to receive and file the August 2022 Parks and Public Works Department update.”
